summary: Melati TUNTASin CHAT feature (patient <-> assigned staff) tested end-to-end. Backend: 11/11 pytest tests PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_chat.py covering patient send/list/unread + hours+clinic_name payload, staff conversations (ordering: unread first, then last_at desc), staff thread + reply, read-receipt logic (patient unread cleared on GET /patient/messages, staff unread cleared on GET /staff/patients/{id}/messages, and other party's unread bumped on send), role enforcement (patient endpoints -> 403 for staff and vice versa, missing token -> 401), and staff access to unassigned patient -> 404 for both GET and POST. Regression: previous 24 backend tests still applicable (not re-run this iteration but no server.py chat changes touched other routes). Frontend (Expo web, mobile viewport 390x844): (1) Patient flow: login pasien/1234 -> Bantuan tab -> tap 'Chat Petugas' card (testID help-chat) -> chat screen opens with header 'Chat Petugas / Puskesmas Melati', chat-hours-banner visible showing 'Jam layanan chat: 08.00-14.00 WIB (hari kerja)...', typed message via chat-input + chat-send appears as right-aligned green bubble, input cleared post-send. (2) Staff flow: login petugas/1234 -> Dashboard shows header-chat with numeric unread badge '1', tap -> chat-daftar screen (testID chatlist) lists 22 conversations, convo with unread (Budi Wijaya) sorted to top with red badge, tap convo-<patientId> -> chat-percakapan renders full thread with patient bubbles left / staff bubbles right, chat-refresh and chat-back present, reply via chat-send appears and persists. Post-open, back on the list, that patient's unread badge is gone (read-receipt reflected). No red-screen errors, no deprecated Expo packages introduced. Only pre-existing benign warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' from react-native-web internals.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py chat routes cleanly project MongoDB _id via {"_id": 0} everywhere; audit trail written on both send paths.
Conversation ordering in /staff/conversations uses two-pass Python sort (last_at desc then unread-first stable). Correct for 22 patients; if roster grows, prefer a single aggregation pipeline.
MessageBody validation: empty text is rejected (422). Only concern: text is not upper-bounded server-side; consider a Pydantic max_length (e.g. 2000) to protect against oversized inputs.

Frontend chat.tsx (~280 lines) is well-scoped, uses KeyboardAvoidingView (from react-native-keyboard-controller), react-query with proper invalidation of ['patient-messages'|'staff-messages',patientId], ['patient-unread']|['staff-unread'], and ['staff-conversations'] on send. Good.
Bantuan Chat card and Dashboard header-chat both wire unread queries; visible badge confirmed on staff dashboard (patient card badge shown as '0' after read as expected in current test session).
One thread per patient keyed by patient_id is enforced at the schema/query level (no thread_id needed). Confirmed by GET returning the same ordered thread regardless of sender.
seed_data_creation: No seed added. Test messages tagged with TEST_ prefix and UI_TEST_ prefix were sent during testing to exercise threads for the demo 'pasien' account (patient_id=Budi Wijaya). These are compatible with normal app usage and can be left as-is; if a clean slate is desired, remove messages where sender_id='<pasien user id>' or where text starts with TEST_ / UI_TEST_.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Chat threads now exist for the demo 'pasien' user (Budi Wijaya, TB-2025001) with a mix of patient and staff messages including TEST_/UI_TEST_ tagged ones. Other 21 seeded patients still have empty threads (label 'Belum ada pesan'). Staff header-chat badge count depends on unread patient messages currently in the DB; expect small fluctuations between runs. To force an unread state for retesting: log in as pasien, send a message via /api/patient/messages, then log in as petugas -- badge >=1 and Budi Wijaya row will float to top with red badge.
